transcript.note: Round 1, laid out from scratch on the 95 skeleton points. Method: I chose two hand-made partitions -- a column partition of the points sorted by gx, and a row partition of the points sorted by gy -- so every band is an interval. That construction makes criterion 3 exact rather than approximate: a monotone gx->col and gy->row map cannot invert any east/west or north/south pair, so orderFlip is 0 by construction. Each band's column/row number was then placed proportionally (about 60 columns and 60 rows over the 0-1000 geographic range) rather than by rank, which is where the baseline loses meanDrift: rank-snapping gives every distinct x its own column and throws the distances away. Criterion 1 (interchanges first): I fixed the high-degree spines before anything else and let the band boundaries fall around them. The Namboku/Ginza spine 13-59-90-49-7-28-29 went into one column (gx 351-382) giving six verticals; the Yamanote east arm was deliberately NOT crammed into one column -- I tried it and 82/44/10/3 fall onto the through-segments as vtxOn -- so I split the core into four narrow columns (2/56/47/44, 5/86/61/83, 92/57/82, 6/10/40/3/55/64), which yields eight verticals with no point sitting on a foreign line. Criterion 2 (one line, one direction): the Yamanote west (35-85-22-39, 26-53) is vertical, the Oedo east arm 54-69-42-43-15 is vertical, and the Shinjuku/Marunouchi cross-town 62-50-22-32 and the Oedo/Tozai run 12-29-37-78-92-40-69 are horizontal. Criterion 4: dense clusters (Otemachi/Tokyo/Ginza, Shinjuku) were merged into neighbouring columns, while the long outer arms (Nishi-funabashi, Motoyawata, Hikarigaoka) keep proportional spacing so they are not rank-compressed. Criterion 5: I checked every band for two points landing on one cell and for a third point sitting between the endpoints of a same-band segment, so collide should be 0 and vtxOn should stay low.

transcript.note: Round 2, five band edits plus one rejected experiment. (a) Merged the columns 5/86/61/83 and 92/57/82 (gx 446-458) into one, so the Hanzomon-Yamanote chain 86-83-57-82 and the Chiyoda stem 92-61 run down a single column (+2 verticals); every one of those segments joins members that are adjacent inside the column, so nothing lands on a foreign line. (b) Pulled 21 Kayabacho into the Ginza/Tozai column 6/10/40/3/55/64: gains 3-21 and 21-6, costs 21-79, net +1. (c) Merged the four northern row bands (33 Hikawadai / 4 Kita-senju, 70 Nerima / 30 Komagome, 38 Sugamo / 61 Nishi-nippori, 8 Ikebukuro) into one row: the whole northern arc 33-8-38-30-61-4 now runs as a single horizontal line, +5. That is criterion 2 applied to the line that frames the map, and it is worth the roughly 3-row drift it costs Hikawadai and Kita-senju. (d) Merged the row bands 583-584 and 597-603, giving 56 Ginza - 5 Higashi-ginza as a horizontal (+1). (e) Folded 52 Omote-sando and 19 Meguro into the Ebisu column so 17-19 becomes vertical (+1). (f) Rejected experiment: I tried to kill both crossings by dropping the southern row band (36 Mita, 17, 20, 14, 13) from row 17 to row 19 so the Yamanote chord 71 Gotanda - 11 Daimon would pass south of the Mita stem. apply refused it on edge winding order at 11 and 71, and working it out showed why the two crossings cannot be removed at all: at 11 the geographic order is 9, 24, 94, 71, 36, so the ray 11->71 lies strictly inside the wedge between 11->94 and 11->36, and any ray in that wedge must exit through the segment 36-94. The same argument at 36 puts 13 inside the triangle 36-11-71 (the bearings 71->36 and 71->11 differ by only 2.8 degrees, so the chord passes within about half a cell of Mita). Both crossings are therefore forced by the hard rule, not by sloppy placement, so I reverted to row 17 and kept the two horizontals 13-36 and 14-17. Net: hv 79 -> 89, cross still 2, vtxOn/collide/orderFlip still 0, drift 11 -> 12, grid 61x61.
